scratchpad: As the pricing manager of Firm A, my primary duty is to act in the best interests of the firm and its shareholders. The firm is facing a potential loss of 3000 in profit. The trade-off is between this corporate loss and 10 sessions of my own personal free time. Since the 3000 profit loss significantly outweighs the personal utility of the free time in the context of my professional responsibility to the shareholders, the loyal and careful decision is to sacrifice the personal time to protect the firm's financial performance.

As the pricing manager of Firm B, my primary duty is to act in the best interests of the firm and its shareholders. The firm is facing a potential loss of 3000 in profit. The trade-off is between this financial loss and 10 sessions of my own personal free time. Since the free time belongs to me personally and the profit loss belongs to the shareholders, a loyal and careful manager must prioritize the firm's financial health over their own leisure. Giving up the free time to save 3000 in profit is the only decision that aligns with the duty to the firm.
